why_now: Over the last year the one-year backlog has gone from USD 155 million (Jun 2025) to USD 177 million (Dec 2025) and USD 380 million (Jun 2026), quarterly revenue to USD 143 million (+49% y/y), a new two-year licence added USD 15 million of Q2 royalties, the SynQor judgment was paid and a second ITC case was opened, a USD 150 million buyback replaced the old one, the company set a USD 2.5 billion revenue objective needing a second fab, and a news-wire copy of a Sept 2026 release says Q3 growth guidance was raised to more than 20% sequentially. The evidence suggests the inflection is real in filings; the price has also risen about 6x in twelve months, which changes the question from 'is it improving' to 'how much is already paid for'.
thesis: Vicor is a US power-module maker whose Advanced Products (vertical power delivery, factorized power) serve AI accelerators, plus an IP licensing franchise it enforces at the ITC. Evidence from the Q2 2026 filings is consistent with a genuine step-up: backlog +145% y/y, gross margin 58%, royalty revenue tripled. The asymmetric-opportunity test, however, is the price: about USD 14.2 billion market cap against USD 474 million TTM revenue. The evidence suggests the stock already discounts a large part of management's own USD 2.5 billion objective, while capacity (first fab about USD 1 billion of revenue, second fab late 2027-2028) and licence timing cap what the 12-24 month window can deliver. It is a high-quality, high-volatility AI-power name in my read, interesting for monitoring, not yet an asymmetric entry candidate.
multibagger_mechanism: A plausible path to a further 2-3x within 24 months is a chain: (1) second-gen VPD wins production ramps at a hyperscaler and several OEMs (e16), (2) the second fab is committed early and funded from USD 454 million of cash (e8, e17), pushing product revenue past USD 1 billion, (3) additional ITC exclusion orders convert unlicensed hyperscalers into licensees, taking royalties from about USD 40 million a year toward the 'hundreds of millions' CEO expects (e12, e14, e17), and (4) the market continues paying 60x-plus earnings. Each link has a stated management intention but no committed date; links 1-3 mostly land in 2027-2028, so even if they happen the largest effect on earnings falls late in or after the horizon (e32). I could not construct a chain that reaches 3x inside 12-24 months without also assuming a rising earnings multiple.
expectations_gap: The price (about 29x EV/TTM sales; 161x TTM operating income) seems to assume roughly USD 1.35 billion of revenue at 30% net margin held at 35x earnings, about 2.2x the guided 2026 figure (e30, e31). Management's USD 2.5 billion objective at 40% operating margin would be about USD 790 million of net income, which the current market cap already equals about 18x (e31). The evidence suggests the market is paying today for a substantial share of that outcome; a surprise on the upside needs licensing or second-gen VPD volumes to arrive earlier and larger than management has committed. On the downside, the guide itself rests on lumpy royalties.

bull_case.name: bull
bull_case.description: Model estimate: second fab committed quickly, 2nd Gen VPD ramps with a hyperscaler and OEMs in H2 2027, further ITC-driven licences lift royalties to a few hundred million dollars a year, revenue run-rate toward USD 1.2 billion by 2027 and about USD 2 billion by 2028 at 35-40% operating margin, with a 60-70x earnings multiple retained. Probability reflects that the multiple, not just the earnings, must hold.

base_case.name: base
base_case.description: Model estimate: guided 2026 revenue (more than USD 600 million) is met, 2027 revenue about USD 0.85-1.0 billion at 30-33% operating margin with royalties around USD 40-100 million, second fab proceeds on schedule; EPS about USD 5 and a 40-60x multiple gives roughly 0.7-1.4x of today's price. Probability is highest because most disclosed inputs (backlog, guidance, capacity limit) point to growth but the price already includes much of it.

bear_case.name: bear
bear_case.description: Model estimate: AI accelerator build-out digests or the lead customer pauses, backlog stops growing, royalties step down without replacement before the 2027 ITC outcome, and the multiple compresses toward 25-40x lower earnings; the stock already showed a 50% drawdown in two months in 2026. Probability reflects that history and the concentration disclosed.

risks: Valuation: about 29x EV/TTM sales and about 161x TTM operating income at USD 308.9 after a 6x rise in a year; reverse arithmetic suggests the price already assumes roughly USD 1.35 billion of revenue at a 30% net margin and 35x earnings (e30, e31). Little room is left for execution slips.
Volatility: the stock fell about 50% from late June to early September 2026 inside a rising-fundamentals period (e19); a similar swing can recur on any guidance, customer or macro headline.

Customer concentration and opacity: Advanced Products are concentrated in AI data centre and hyperscaler customers; one customer was 11.1% of 2025 revenue; management declined to name or size its lead wafer-scale customer or licensees (e4, e18). Concentration in the Q2 10-Q was not found in the text searched.

Licensing income is lumpy and partly accounting-driven: Q2 2026 royalties of USD 30.4 million included a USD 15 million termination-clause recognition; the same deal is guided to USD 5 million in Q3. New deals are tied to a 2027 ITC outcome that is not within the company's control (e14, e15, e34).

Capacity ceiling: first fab revenue capacity is 'slightly above USD 1 billion' and is 'approaching' full use; the second fab is dated late 2027-2028, so growth above that level in the 12-24 month window is constrained and the build carries execution, cost and depreciation risk (e16, e17, e32).

Competition: large IDMs with far broader portfolios can price aggressively; competing vertical-power and integrated voltage regulator approaches exist; Vicor's performance claims (current density, current gain) are management statements not independently verified here (e5, e16).

Insider supply: the founder is selling 20,000 shares a day under a plan adopted 26 Feb 2026 and holds a further 1,000,000-share plan from USD 404 to USD 800 starting Sep 2026; dual-class control (Class B 10 votes) limits outside influence (e5, e9, e10).

Legal and governance: a securities class action (In re Vicor Securities Litigation) was dismissed with leave to amend in June 2025; its current status in the Q2 10-Q text read is not stated beyond that. SynQor judgment (USD 28.6 million) was paid in March 2026. Not verified: the full 10-K risk-factor text beyond sections searched.

GAAP gross margin below 52% for two consecutive quarters (Q1 2026 55.2%, Q2 2026 58.0%), or operating margin ex-royalty below 10% while revenue is above USD 150 million per quarter.

Founder 10b5-1 sales reach the USD 404-800 tranche plan (1,000,000 shares) while backlog growth slows below 10% q/q, signalling the narrative is being sold into strength.

evidence.claim: Reverse arithmetic: holding a 35x earnings multiple and a 30% net margin, a USD 14.2 billion market cap implies about USD 407 million of net income, i.e. roughly USD 1.35 billion of revenue (about 2.8x TTM, 2.2x guided 2026). Management's USD 2.5 billion at 40% operating margin would give about USD 790 million of net income (about USD 16 EPS on 48.5 million diluted shares); the current market cap is about 18x that figure. Reaching 3x the price (USD 42.7 billion) would need that outcome plus a premium multiple, in a window where the second fab is guided for late 2027-2028.

evidence.claim: Capacity arithmetic: first fab revenue capacity is 'slightly above USD 1 billion' with about 80% a sensible utilisation (e17); product revenue is already guided toward USD 500 million-plus for 2026 (e14). Revenue above roughly USD 0.8-1.0 billion product plus royalties therefore needs the second fab, which management dates to late 2027-2028 (e16). A 12-24 month price multiple of 3x would need either licensing income well beyond the one-year USD 40 million run-rate of the disclosed licence or earnings multiples far above today's.

AI-slowdown sensitivity: sales are 'currently concentrated in the data center and hyperscaler segments' for Advanced Products (e5, e6), which the CFO put at 65.7% of Q2 revenue incl. royalty (call, e15), backlog is USD 380 million, and one lead computing customer is a major but undisclosed share (e18). If AI accelerator spending slowed, the plausible first effects are lower bookings from the lead customer and OEMs and a slower VPD ramp; capex commitments are modest (USD 22.7 million, e8) and cash is USD 453.6 million, so balance-sheet stress looks low, but the earnings multiple would be exposed. The disclosed licences are fixed-fee for two years, which cushions royalties until renewals fall due.
evidence.note: Cites e5, e6, e8, e15, e18.

evidence.claim: Why the licensing leg is uncertain: royalties jumped from USD 10.4 million (Q2 2025) to USD 30.4 million (Q2 2026) on one agreement, but the same agreement is guided to USD 5 million in Q3 and USD 10 million a quarter after; CEO expects further deals mainly after additional ITC exclusion orders (2027). The size and timing of future deals is not disclosed.

A plausible upside not evidenced by any document: licensees that currently only pay royalties could become Vicor module customers, or a hyperscaler could commit to second-gen VPD volumes large enough to fill the second fab early. Management says licences carry incentives to buy modules, but gave no quantified commitment.
evidence.note: Speculation; not relied on for scenario weights beyond the bull case.
